headline.title: Google I/O floods the feed as the AI stack gets picked.
headline.summary: Google I/O 2026 dominates the day with Gemini Spark, Gemini Omni, Project Genie and a cross-lab SynthID watermark, while AMD ships the first 2nm HPC chip and Anthropic's Claude Mythos finds 10,000 vulnerabilities in a month. Underneath the product noise sit hard numbers on AI economics: Microsoft's token bills now exceed salaries, DeepSeek cements a 75% price cut, and Google's monthly token volume is up 330x in two years. The optionality of the last two years is closing as the industry settles on defaults for compute, geography, provenance and policy.

stories.title: AMD ships the industry's first 2nm HPC chip, beating NVIDIA to the node.
stories.toc_summary: AMD ramps its 6th-gen EPYC Venice on TSMC's 2nm node — the first HPC-class processor on 2nm, ahead of NVIDIA and Intel.
stories.quick_take: AMD has begun the production ramp of its 6th-generation EPYC processor, codenamed Venice, on TSMC's 2nm node, making it the first HPC-class processor in the industry to enter production on 2nm [1]. Venice packs 256 cores per socket on the Zen 6 architecture, delivers more than 70% better performance and efficiency than the current Turin generation, and adds a 30% increase in thread density [1]. A follow-on chip called Verano is already on the roadmap with industry-leading LPDDR integration aimed at memory-hungry agentic AI workloads [1]. AMD positioned the launch explicitly against agentic compute demand rather than raw FLOPS [1].

bullets.label: First to the node:
bullets.text: Apple has reportedly locked up most early TSMC N2 capacity for consumer chips; Venice is the first publicly announced HPC product to ramp on it, putting AMD ahead of NVIDIA, Intel and the rest of the data-center field [1].

bullets.label: Densest server CPU yet:
bullets.text: 256 cores per socket on Zen 6 is the densest server CPU ever announced, and combined with the 70% efficiency gain it pushes the data-center perf-per-watt curve past last year's projections [1].

bullets.label: Built for agents:
bullets.text: The roadmap is now written against the agent compute curve — Verano integrates LPDDR specifically for memory-heavy agentic tasks [1].

bullets.label: The NVIDIA frame:
bullets.text: NVIDIA owns the GPU side of AI compute; AMD just took the CPU side into the 2nm era first, sharpening the hyperscaler buying conversation ahead of NVIDIA's next earnings call [1].

callout.label: THE BIG PICTURE
callout.text: Three weeks after Jensen Huang put a 1,000% number on agentic compute demand and Blackstone put $25B behind it, AMD shipped the first HPC chip on a 2nm node [1]. The substrate of AI is getting denser, faster and more contested at every layer [1].

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude Mythos finds over 10,000 vulnerabilities in one month.
stories.toc_summary: Anthropic's closed Project Glasswing used the unreleased Claude Mythos model to surface 10,000+ critical bugs across 50 partners in a single month.
stories.quick_take: Anthropic published one-month results from Project Glasswing, a closed cybersecurity initiative built around Claude Mythos Preview, an unreleased frontier model [1]. In one month, around 50 partners — including Microsoft, Apple, Google, AWS, Cloudflare, JPMorgan, Cisco, NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks — discovered more than 10,000 high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, cloud platforms, browsers, enterprise software and open-source projects [1]. Cloudflare alone reported 2,000 vulnerabilities, and Mozilla used the model to patch 271 issues in Firefox 150, roughly a 10x jump over prior Claude testing [1]. Anthropic claims a false-positive rate below that of human security testers [1].

bullets.label: Order-of-magnitude scale:
bullets.text: 10,000 high- and critical-severity bugs in one month is far faster than any prior security research effort, spanning more than 1,000 open-source projects [1].

bullets.label: Deliberately contained:
bullets.text: Anthropic withheld Mythos from public release because the same capability that finds vulnerabilities can write exploits; the UK AI Security Institute confirmed Mythos is the first model to fully solve its multi-step cyberattack simulations [1].

bullets.label: The Firefox datapoint:
bullets.text: Mozilla found 271 vulnerabilities with Mythos versus roughly 27 in prior Claude testing — a 10x scan-productivity jump on the same product likely to repeat across Chrome, Safari and enterprise platforms [1].

bullets.label: Live defense, not just pen-testing:
bullets.text: Anthropic says Mythos helped one banking partner detect and prevent a $1.5M fraudulent wire transfer after attackers compromised a customer's email [1].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: One month, 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities, 50 partners — the defense-offense balance in cybersecurity just tilted measurably, and whoever holds Mythos-class access holds the advantage [1].

sources.title: StayingAhead Daily Digest, Issue 021 — Anthropic Project Glasswing one-month report

stories.title: SynthID becomes the cross-lab AI watermarking standard.
stories.toc_summary: At Google I/O 2026, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao and ElevenLabs all adopt Google's SynthID watermark, with verification rolling into Search and Chrome.
stories.quick_take: At Google I/O 2026, Sundar Pichai confirmed that OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao and ElevenLabs are adopting Google's SynthID watermark for AI-generated content [1]. SynthID embeds imperceptible signals into images, video, audio and text; verification is rolling into Google Search immediately and into Chrome within weeks [1]. Google says SynthID has already watermarked over 100 billion images and videos plus 60,000 years of audio [1]. OpenAI confirmed it is becoming C2PA-conformant in parallel and adding SynthID to images from ChatGPT, Codex and its API [1].

bullets.label: A Schelling point at last:
bullets.text: With OpenAI, NVIDIA, Google, ElevenLabs and Kakao on the same invisible signal, the industry has picked a default; remaining holdouts Anthropic, Meta and xAI become the exception, not the rule [1].

bullets.label: Verification at the point of consumption:
bullets.text: Search and Chrome checks move provenance from the point of creation to the point of viewing — the bar to verify an AI image drops from 'open the Gemini app' to 'right-click in browser' [1].

bullets.label: Two layers, two failure modes:
bullets.text: SynthID survives compression and screenshots; C2PA carries strippable but human-readable cryptographic creator metadata. OpenAI is shipping both for robustness [1].

bullets.label: Shipping volume, not a claim:
bullets.text: 100 billion watermarked images and videos is production scale — once Chrome ships verification, every AI image on the open web becomes traceable to its source model [1].

callout.label: WHAT THIS CHANGES
callout.text: If you build with AI-generated media in any commercial context, your output is now traceable to your model by default — easing brand safety, contract compliance and IP work, and finally giving deepfake defense a real toolset [1].

sources.title: StayingAhead Daily Digest, Issue 021 — Google I/O 2026

stories.title: OpenAI opens its first Applied AI Lab outside the US in Singapore.
stories.toc_summary: OpenAI commits ~US$234M to a Singapore Applied AI Lab under an MDDI partnership, planning 200+ technical roles and a Forward-Deployed Engineers hub.
stories.quick_take: OpenAI committed more than S$300 million (about US$234 million) to Singapore under a partnership with the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, establishing the OpenAI Singapore Applied AI Lab — its first such lab outside the United States [1]. Plans include growing the local technical team to more than 200 roles over the next few years and making Singapore a global hub for Forward-Deployed Engineers [1]. The lab focuses on public services, finance, healthcare and digital infrastructure [1].

bullets.label: Following traction, not flags:
bullets.text: OpenAI passed over Tokyo, Seoul and Bangalore; Singapore is top-three globally in per-capita ChatGPT adoption and top-five in Codex usage [1].

bullets.label: The Palantir playbook:
bullets.text: Forward-Deployed Engineers — staff embedded inside customer organizations to deploy frontier AI on operational problems — now get a second hub outside San Francisco [1].

bullets.label: A government co-signer:
bullets.text: The MDDI partnership gives OpenAI policy access, a public-sector pipeline and an aligned regulatory partner; the closest comparable is Microsoft's UAE arrangement [1].

bullets.label: The contested market:
bullets.text: Google announced an expanded Singapore AI partnership the same week, and Microsoft and AWS already have deep local presence, making Singapore the most contested non-US AI policy market [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: If you sell B2B AI tools into APAC, treat Singapore as your wedge market rather than Japan or India — the buying signal is strongest, the policy environment most stable, and per-capita paid-AI adoption is already there [1].

sources.title: StayingAhead Daily Digest, Issue 021 — OpenAI for Singapore announcement

stories.title: The White House pulls back on federal frontier-model vetting.
stories.toc_summary: Key parts of the federal AI executive order requiring frontier-model security vetting are postponed, with Musk and Zuckerberg pushing back on competitiveness grounds.
stories.quick_take: The White House has postponed or scrapped key parts of the federal AI executive order that would have required frontier-model security vetting and government-shared safety reports [1]. Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg both pushed back publicly, arguing the framework would slow US deployment relative to China, and the administration cited competitiveness as its rationale [1]. The retreat continues a pattern: California signed an AI workforce executive order two days earlier, while Washington has now stepped back from federal-level AI safety review [1].

bullets.label: Floor reverts to voluntary:
bullets.text: With mandatory frontier-model vetting pulled, the federal AI safety floor effectively returns to the 2023 OpenAI-Anthropic-Google voluntary pledges as the binding US standard [1].

bullets.label: A rare lobbying alignment:
bullets.text: Musk and Zuckerberg opposing the same federal AI policy is unusual, and their posture aligns with most of the lab-CEO bench — industry consensus moved the needle in days [1].

bullets.label: Everything framed as China:
bullets.text: Each retreat is now justified on competitiveness with China, a framing likely to beat safety arguments by default for the rest of this administration [1].

bullets.label: States now matter more:
bullets.text: With the federal layer stepping back, the 50-state map dominates; California's October 2026 worker-impact deadline is the next concrete milestone, with Texas, New York and Florida next to watch [1].

callout.label: WATCH NEXT
callout.text: Two policy clocks are running: California's AI workforce recommendations land October 2026 while the federal EO timeline is now blank — whichever state acts next becomes the de facto US AI regulator through 2028 [1].

stories.title: Google's Gemini Spark turns the assistant into a 24/7 autonomous agent.
stories.toc_summary: Announced at I/O 2026, Gemini Spark runs on a dedicated Google Cloud VM, works while your devices are off, and composes Tasks, Skills and Schedules across nine Workspace apps.
stories.quick_take: Gemini Spark is Google's new personal AI agent, announced at I/O 2026, that works in the background 24/7 even when your phone is locked, your laptop is shut or you are offline [1]. It runs on dedicated virtual machines in Google Cloud, powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and Google's Antigravity tool-use harness, and completes entire workflows rather than just answering prompts [1]. Spark is built around three primitives — Tasks (jobs you assign), Skills (reusable behaviors taught in plain language) and Schedules (time- or condition-based triggers) — that compose to define everything it can do [1]. It integrates natively with nine Google Workspace apps plus live MCP partners Canva, OpenTable and Instacart, with Spotify and Adobe landing through summer 2026 [1].

bullets.label: Always-on architecture:
bullets.text: Spark runs on its own Google Cloud VM, so your local device can be off while it keeps working — closing the gap between AI suggestion and AI execution [1].

bullets.label: Teachable Skills are the killer feature:
bullets.text: Tell Spark to read your last 50 sent emails and extract your writing style into a permanent Ghostwriter Skill, and every future draft uses it automatically — no code or fine-tuning [1].

bullets.label: Schedules add autonomy:
bullets.text: A Monday-9am schedule can fire a Task that calls your Skim and Planning Skills so you wake up to a finished briefing; other examples include monthly invoicing and auto-flagging hidden subscriptions [1].

bullets.label: Opt-in by default:
bullets.text: Every connection starts off, Spark only reads what you direct it to, and it asks before spending money or sending external email — the granular permission model agents should have [1].

bullets.label: Access path:
bullets.text: Currently in trusted-tester rollout; public beta is next for Google AI Ultra subscribers ($249.99/month, 18+, US only), with a macOS desktop app already available [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: The next 18 months of personal productivity will accrue to people who teach an agent their style and schedule — build a Ghostwriter Skill and set one recurring schedule now, because the compounding starts immediately at near-zero marginal cost [1].

stories.title: Microsoft's internal numbers show AI tokens costing more than salaries.
stories.toc_summary: Leaked internal Microsoft reports show per-employee token and agent-workflow costs exceeding salaries, turning the AI rollout into an unbudgeted cost center.
stories.quick_take: Internal Microsoft reports reveal what many companies are feeling: the more employees use AI tools, the harder the bill, with token consumption and agent workflows summing per head to amounts that exceed salaries [1][2]. Microsoft had sold its own AI rollout as an efficiency lever, but the token economy has become a cost center no one had budgeted [1]. The pressure pushes downward toward cheaper models, harder caching strategies and smaller agent loops [1].

bullets.label: The uncomfortable inversion:
bullets.text: When per-employee AI spend tops the salary that employee is paid, the productivity narrative collides with the unit economics [1].

bullets.label: Who captures the value:
bullets.text: Pouring AI unfiltered into workflows can end up financing a model vendor's margins rather than your own productivity [1].

bullets.label: The cost-control response:
bullets.text: Expect a shift toward cheaper or open-weight models, aggressive caching and tighter agent loops to contain spend [1].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: Microsoft's numbers are a warning shot for every enterprise: AI deployment without cost governance can quietly invert the business case it was meant to prove [1].

sources.title: KI Bubble — 'Microsoft zahlt für KI mehr als für eigene Mitarbeiter'

stories.title: DeepSeek makes its 75% V4 Pro price cut permanent.
stories.toc_summary: DeepSeek permanently drops V4 Pro to $0.43/M input and $0.87/M output tokens, with near-free caching, on the back of a 27% compute reduction.
stories.quick_take: DeepSeek has made its discount permanent: V4 Pro now costs $0.43 per million input tokens and $0.87 per million output tokens, with cache effectively free at $0.003625 [1]. The company's technical paper justifies the move with 27% less compute and only 10% of the cache consumption compared with V3.2 [1]. While OpenAI sells capacity in year-long contracts and Microsoft chokes on its own token bills, China is pushing efficiency up and prices toward marginal cost [1].

bullets.label: Concrete new floor:
bullets.text: $0.43/$0.87 per million tokens with near-free caching resets price expectations for capable models [1].

bullets.label: Efficiency, not subsidy:
bullets.text: The 27% compute reduction and 10% cache use versus V3.2 are presented as the engineering basis for the permanent cut [1].

bullets.label: ROI bar drops again:
bullets.text: For DACH teams migrating workflows onto open-weight models, the threshold for a positive return falls noticeably [1].

callout.label: THE BIG PICTURE
callout.text: The pricing war has two strategies on display: Western labs locking in capacity contracts, and Chinese labs driving efficiency to crush per-token cost — and the second is winning on price [1].

stories.title: Google's monthly token volume grows 330x in twenty-four months.
stories.toc_summary: Per Sundar Pichai at I/O 2026, Google's monthly token throughput went from 9.7T (May 2024) to 480T to 3,200T (May 2026) — the new baseline load for Search, Workspace and Gemini.
stories.quick_take: Sundar Pichai disclosed at Google I/O 2026 that Google's monthly token throughput rose from 9.7 trillion in May 2024 to about 480 trillion a year later and to 3,200 trillion today — a factor of 330 in 24 months [1][2]. This is not just growth but the new baseline load for Search, Workspace and the Gemini models, as every query once answered with a link now runs through a model and costs tokens [1][2]. Both the Everlast and KI Bubble newsletters flagged the same chart as the day's standout datapoint [1][2].

bullets.label: The numbers:
bullets.text: 9.7T → 480T → 3,200T monthly tokens across May 2024, May 2025 and May 2026 — a 330x jump in two years [1][2].

bullets.label: From links to inference:
bullets.text: Every request that used to return a hyperlink now passes through a model, turning inference into the platform's permanent base load [1].

bullets.label: The new question:
bullets.text: For everyone outside the hyperscalers, the framing shifts from 'how much AI do we use?' to 'how much compute can we afford?' [1].

callout.label: THE LONG ARC
callout.text: Whoever orchestrates compute at this scale builds the infrastructure the next software generation runs on — and 330x in 24 months shows that base load compounding in real time [1].

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni for conversational video editing.
stories.toc_summary: Gemini Omni brings the Nano-Banana conversational model to video — deliver a clip, type an instruction, get edits to cut, style and scene changes back, by voice.
stories.quick_take: Google is extending the Nano-Banana conversational-editing principle to moving images with a new model called Gemini Omni [1]. Omni generates and edits video in dialogue: supply a clip, type or speak an instruction, and get the result back, with cuts, style and scene changes driven entirely by language [1]. This puts Google directly into the post-production lane where Veo previously acted only as a generator [1].

bullets.label: Edit, don't just generate:
bullets.text: Omni iterates on existing footage in the same session rather than only producing new clips, attacking the editing workflow head-on [1].

bullets.label: Language as the interface:
bullets.text: Cutting, restyling and scene swaps run through conversational instructions, lowering the skill barrier for video work [1].

bullets.label: Stack implications:
bullets.text: Anyone using AI for short-form, ad clips or reels now has to benchmark their stack against a model that both generates and refines [1].

callout.label: WHAT TO WATCH
callout.text: If conversational editing proves reliable on real footage, the gap between AI 'generation' tools and full editing suites narrows fast [1].

stories.title: Project Genie turns any Street View location into a walkable simulation.
stories.toc_summary: Google DeepMind's Project Genie now plugs into Google Maps Street View, generating navigable interactive 3D worlds from panorama imagery of real US locations.
stories.quick_take: Google DeepMind's Project Genie now docks into Google Maps Street View, letting any real US location be turned into a walkable, interactive 3D world generated from the panorama imagery Google has collected for years [1]. What used to live in academic demos suddenly sits atop a dataset of billions of mapped streets [1]. A model that processes every pixel of the physical world as input and produces consistent navigable spaces becomes a universal simulation layer [1].

bullets.label: Demo to data scale:
bullets.text: Genie jumps from research curiosity to a base of billions of real-world panorama captures in one move [1].

bullets.label: A simulation substrate:
bullets.text: Consistent, navigable spaces generated from real imagery form a layer agents can train in and creators can build on [1].

bullets.label: Who uses it:
bullets.text: Agents train, film studios scout and game developers build inside it without ever touching a polygon engine [1].

callout.label: THE LONG ARC
callout.text: World models grounded in real Street View data point toward training and content pipelines that no longer need hand-built 3D environments [1].

stories.title: GPT-5.5 Pro builds a full CAD model of the ISS from a prompt.
stories.toc_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro generates a complete parametric 3D model of the International Space Station in ForgeCAD — solar panels, modules and docking ports — from a prompt.
stories.quick_take: GPT-5.5 Pro generated a complete 3D model of the International Space Station in ForgeCAD, with solar panels, modules and docking ports all parametrically constructed [1]. Work that previously cost weeks of CAD effort now runs from a prompt, as the line between language model and engineering tool blurs [1]. The model understands spatial geometry, hierarchies and part relationships well enough to drive industrial CAD workflows directly [1].

bullets.label: Parametric, not just a render:
bullets.text: The ISS model is built with real CAD structure — panels, modules and docking points as parametric components [1].

bullets.label: Weeks to minutes:
bullets.text: A task that needed dedicated CAD engineers for concept models collapses into a few sentences of prompt [1].

bullets.label: A break for hardware teams:
bullets.text: Teams that relied on a full design office for concept geometry can now get usable output from a description [1].

callout.label: WHAT TO WATCH
callout.text: If language models can reliably emit valid parametric CAD, concept engineering becomes a prompt-first workflow and the bottleneck shifts to validation [1].

stories.title: EngineAI rolls a humanoid off the line every fifteen minutes.
stories.toc_summary: EngineAI's new 10,000-unit T800 line in Shenzhen is officially producing humanoids full-stack in-house, at exactly 15 minutes per unit.
stories.quick_take: EngineAI's new 10,000-unit line for the T800 humanoid is running in Shenzhen Honghualing, with the first batch officially off the line and the full stack in-house: R&D, manufacturing, quality control and delivery [1]. The upgraded line delivers 40% more output, runs 79 full-quality checks per robot and simulates 46 working conditions, producing exactly one humanoid every 15 minutes from kit to finished unit [1]. The viral 'kick-the-CEO' T800 becomes the first serious production story out of China [1].

bullets.label: Real production cadence:
bullets.text: 15 minutes per humanoid, kit to finished unit, on a line built for 10,000 units [1].

bullets.label: Full-stack and in-house:
bullets.text: R&D, fabrication, QC and delivery all sit under one roof, with 79 quality checks and 46 simulated working conditions per robot [1].

bullets.label: From demo to volume:
bullets.text: The conversation about humanoids shifts from viral demo videos to unit counts [1].

callout.label: THE BIG PICTURE
callout.text: China just produced the first credible humanoid manufacturing-throughput story, moving the robotics debate from capability clips to production economics [1].

stories.title: Tesla opens its Fremont hall for one million Optimus robots a year.
stories.toc_summary: At the final Model S/X handover, Tesla opened the Fremont hall slated to build Optimus from next year at a planned one-million-units-per-year capacity.
stories.quick_take: At the handover of the last Model S and X, Tesla opened the doors to the hall where Optimus is to be built starting next year, with planned capacity of one million units annually [1]. Designer Franz von Holzhausen said the space would soon be 'full of robots,' while Elon Musk quipped that at the next handover 'Optimus hands itself over' [1]. Fremont was North America's most productive auto factory four years running [1].

bullets.label: Million-a-year target:
bullets.text: Tesla is positioning Fremont for one million Optimus units per year from next year [1].

bullets.label: Repurposing proven capacity:
bullets.text: The site that led North American auto production for four years is being turned toward humanoid hardware [1].

bullets.label: Western counterweight:
bullets.text: From 2027 the hall is meant to ship more humanoid hardware than anywhere else in the Western hemisphere [1].

callout.label: WHAT TO WATCH
callout.text: Paired with EngineAI's 15-minute cadence, Tesla's million-unit plan signals that the 2027 robotics race is about manufacturing capacity, not just capability [1].

stories.title: ChatGPT now fills out forms by voice from a photo.
stories.toc_summary: OpenAI fuses image upload and Voice Mode: photograph a form, talk through the answers, and get the completed document back — three modalities in one pass.
stories.quick_take: OpenAI has linked image upload and Voice Mode into a single workflow: upload a photo of a form, speak through what goes in each field, and receive the completed document back [1]. The real leap is under the hood — the vision model recognizes fields, the voice stack transcribes answers, and the same context writes back into the image, combining three modalities in one pass without switching apps or typing [1]. For freelancers and SMEs this targets tax forms, insurance documents, applications and expense reports [1].

bullets.label: Three modalities, one pass:
bullets.text: Vision field-detection, voice transcription and write-back run together with no app switching or typing [1].

bullets.label: Concrete use cases:
bullets.text: Tax forms, insurance paperwork, applications and travel-expense reports are the named targets [1].

bullets.label: Time reclaimed:
bullets.text: Hours that vanish into bureaucratic PDFs each month shrink to a few minutes of speaking [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: If form-filling eats your admin time, test the photo-plus-voice flow on a recurring document this week — it is the clearest near-term productivity win in today's product news [1].

stories.title: Seven million H100-equivalents sit outside the frontier labs.
stories.toc_summary: The headline AI labs hold a minority of global compute: OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI together ~3.4M H100-equivalents, Google ~4M, and the rest of the world ~7M.
stories.quick_take: When AI is discussed, the same names recur — OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI — but together those three frontier labs hold only about 3.4 million H100-equivalents [1]. Google alone holds roughly 4 million, more than all three combined, and by far the largest block is the ~7 million spread across the rest of the world's cloud providers, corporations and states [1]. The headline labs represent only a small slice of global AI infrastructure [1].

bullets.label: The distribution:
bullets.text: ~3.4M H100-equivalents across OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI; ~4M at Google; ~7M across everyone else [1].

bullets.label: Not a monopoly:
bullets.text: Compute is not concentrated in a handful of labs — there is a broad, growing infrastructure base behind serious AI deployment [1].

bullets.label: Implication for buyers:
bullets.text: Companies committing to AI are not dependent on three labs; the available capacity is far wider than the headlines suggest [1].

callout.label: THE BIG PICTURE
callout.text: The frontier-lab narrative obscures where most AI compute actually lives — outside the labs, in a distributed and expanding global base [1].

sources.title: Everlast AI — 'Charts der Woche: Compute, Köpfe, Klinik'

stories.title: High-bandwidth memory now eats 63% of an AI chip's cost.
stories.toc_summary: Per Epoch AI, HBM's share of AI-chip cost rose from 50% in Q1 2024 to 63% eight quarters later, making memory suppliers the booms's quiet winners.
stories.quick_take: In Q1 2024 half the cost of an AI chip went to high-bandwidth memory; eight quarters later it is 63%, with logic, packaging and everything else splitting the rest, according to Epoch AI [1]. The reason is simple and brutal: every new model generation needs more memory bandwidth per training step [1]. That makes HBM makers SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron the quiet profiteers of the AI boom — whoever gets their stacks builds chips, and whoever misses out builds PowerPoints [1].

bullets.label: The shift:
bullets.text: HBM's share of AI-chip cost climbed from 50% (Q1 2024) to 63% over eight quarters [1].

bullets.label: Bandwidth is the driver:
bullets.text: Each model generation demands more memory bandwidth per training step, pushing memory's cost share up [1].

bullets.label: Where the leverage sits:
bullets.text: The first compute bottleneck is memory supply, not logic — and the lever on compute prices sits in Korea, not Taiwan [1].

callout.label: THE LONG ARC
callout.text: For anyone with an AI-hardware roadmap, HBM allocation — not logic — is the constraint that decides who actually ships chips [1].

sources.title: Everlast AI — 'Charts der Woche' (source: Epoch AI)

stories.title: Superstar AI researchers now earn 500 times a postdoc's salary.
stories.toc_summary: The AI pay ladder runs from ~$50K for a postdoc to $25M for a poached superstar — one of the most extreme salary gradients outside pro sports and hedge funds.
stories.quick_take: A postdoc earns around $50,000 a year, a US tenure-track professor about $250,000, a regular senior researcher at OpenAI around $1 million, and a superstar moved from lab to lab roughly $25 million [1]. The gap from academic entry to the top is not 10x or 100x but about 500x, making AI one of the most extreme salary gradients anywhere — comparable only to pro sports or hedge-fund traders [1]. Behind it is a bet that a handful of researchers decide which lab makes the next leap [1].

bullets.label: The ladder:
bullets.text: ~$50K postdoc → ~$250K professor → ~$1M senior OpenAI researcher → ~$25M poached superstar [1].

bullets.label: Why labs pay it:
bullets.text: If a single hire shortens a training run by weeks, $25M is quickly recouped [1].

bullets.label: The real scarcity:
bullets.text: The genuinely scarce resource in the AI market is not GPUs but the people who can move a model forward [1].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: A 500x spread signals that top research talent, not compute, is the variable labs believe decides the race [1].

sources.title: Everlast AI — 'Charts der Woche: Compute, Köpfe, Klinik'

stories.title: AI users are growing three times faster than AI developers.
stories.toc_summary: Per McKinsey, Europe's AI-using workforce jumped 5x (1.9M to 9.4M) in two years while AI builders grew only 1.7x — the application layer is outpacing technical depth.
stories.quick_take: According to the McKinsey Global Institute's 'Agents, robots, and us' (May 2026), the number of European workers in jobs that use or manage AI jumped from 1.9 million to 9.4 million in two years — a factor of 5.0 [1]. Those who build or steer AI, the classic developer stack, grew only by a factor of 1.7, from 2.0 to 3.3 million [1]. The application layer is thus expanding nearly three times faster than the technical depth [1].

bullets.label: The two curves:
bullets.text: AI users: 1.9M → 9.4M (5.0x); AI developers: 2.0M → 3.3M (1.7x) over two years in Europe [1].

bullets.label: Where the leverage moved:
bullets.text: The biggest lever is no longer model training but the broad workforce applying AI day to day [1].

bullets.label: Strategic read:
bullets.text: Organizations that turn employees into AI users now are positioning for the 2030 growth deck [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: Invest in turning your existing workforce into capable AI users — the data says adoption breadth, not build depth, is where the next wave of value concentrates [1].

sources.title: Everlast AI — 'Charts der Woche' (source: McKinsey Global Institute, 'Agents, robots, and us', May 2026)

stories.title: AI power-user nurses lead clinically by up to 51 points.
stories.toc_summary: A McKinsey survey of 521 nurses finds heavy AI users pull ahead most where care is highest-risk — 51 points on clinical decision support, 50 on medication management.
stories.quick_take: Nurses who use AI intensively pull ahead most exactly where care gets clinically serious, according to the McKinsey Nursing AI Insights Survey 2026 (n=521) [1]. Power-users lead by 51 percentage points on clinical decision support, 50 on medication management and 46 on care-plan personalization [1]. The striking pattern is that the higher the patient risk, the wider the gap: routine workflows like scheduling show a 39-point lead, while sensitive clinical workflows show 42 to 51 [1].

bullets.label: Biggest gaps at highest risk:
bullets.text: 51 points on clinical decision support, 50 on medication management, 46 on care-plan personalization [1].

bullets.label: Risk scales the divide:
bullets.text: Routine tasks show a 39-point gap; sensitive clinical workflows widen to 42-51 points [1].

bullets.label: A widening league:
bullets.text: AI-fluent nurses are building their own tier, and the gap grows where mistakes are most costly [1].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: In healthcare, AI fluency compounds most where stakes are highest — suggesting the adoption gap among clinicians is also a patient-outcome gap [1].

stories.title: A supply-chain attack infects more than 700 GitHub repositories.
stories.toc_summary: Over 700 GitHub repos, including core PHP and Node.js projects, were flooded with malware that hides in package.json and drops a disguised /tmp/.sshd binary.
stories.quick_take: More than 700 GitHub repositories — including central PHP and Node.js projects — were flooded with malicious code [1]. On install, the package quietly pulls a Linux file, disguises it as /tmp/.sshd and executes it, skipping security checks on download and suppressing error messages [1]. Eight PHP packages on Packagist are confirmed infected; the trick is hiding the script in package.json rather than composer.json, exactly where PHP developers do not look [1].

bullets.label: High-profile targets:
bullets.text: devdojo/wave (6,400 stars) and devdojo/genesis (9,100 installs), two popular Laravel templates, are among the affected [1].

bullets.label: CI poisoned too:
bullets.text: A fake build step named 'Dependency Cache Sync' smuggled the payload into corporate GitHub Actions CI pipelines [1].

bullets.label: Evasion by misdirection:
bullets.text: Placing the loader in package.json, suppressing errors and disguising the binary as /tmp/.sshd is built to dodge routine review [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: Audit dependencies and CI build steps for unexpected install-time scripts and any '/tmp/.sshd' artifact — and treat package.json in PHP projects as a place attackers now hide [1].

stories.title: Perplexity open-sources Bumblebee to scan developer machines.
stories.toc_summary: Perplexity releases Bumblebee, a read-only open-source scanner for macOS and Linux that checks dev machines for risky packages, browser extensions and AI-tool configs.
stories.quick_take: Perplexity has open-sourced Bumblebee, a read-only scanner for macOS and Linux that inspects developer machines for risky packages, browser extensions and AI-tool configurations — no writes, no intervention, just an inventory of what is actually running [1]. Its real leverage is integration with Comet, Perplexity's agent: when a new supply-chain threat appears, a deeper scan can be triggered automatically [1]. The arrival lands the same week as the 700-repo GitHub attack, as the supply chain proves to be modern software's soft flank [1].

bullets.label: Read-only by design:
bullets.text: Bumblebee takes inventory without write access, surfacing risky packages, extensions and AI-tool configs [1].

bullets.label: Agent-triggered depth:
bullets.text: Tied to Perplexity's Comet agent, it can auto-launch a deeper scan the moment a new threat emerges [1].

bullets.label: Continuous, not quarterly:
bullets.text: Dev-team attack surface gets checked against the live threat picture rather than once a quarter [1].

callout.label: WHAT TO WATCH
callout.text: An open-source, agent-triggered scanner arriving alongside a 700-repo attack signals the dev-machine supply chain becoming an actively monitored surface [1].

stories.title: Demis Hassabis says the singularity is only a few years away.
stories.toc_summary: The Google DeepMind chief expects true AGI within a few years, calling AI 'the most important technology of all time' — notable because he builds the models in question.
stories.quick_take: Demis Hassabis expects true AGI to arrive within a few years and set the singularity in motion [1]. The Google DeepMind chief calls it 'the most important technology of all time,' more transformative than anything before [1]. What is notable is less the claim than the source: the man building the very model meant to trigger the transition [1].

bullets.label: The timeline:
bullets.text: Hassabis puts real AGI within a few years, with the singularity following [1].

bullets.label: The framing:
bullets.text: He describes AI as the most important and transformative technology in history [1].

bullets.label: Why the source matters:
bullets.text: From a lab chief building the model, the statement reads less as sci-fi and more as a roadmap [1].

callout.label: THE LONG ARC
callout.text: When the person building frontier models puts AGI a few years out, the claim shifts from speculation toward a planning assumption worth taking seriously [1].

stories.title: Voicely pitches GDPR-compliant AI dictation that saves 20 hours a month.
stories.toc_summary: KI Bubble's tool tip: Voicely is a GDPR-compliant dictation app with AI speech recognition that runs in any app, claiming ~20 hours saved per month for heavy writers.
stories.quick_take: KI Bubble's tool recommendation of the day is Voicely, a GDPR-compliant dictation app with AI-assisted speech recognition that runs inside any application [1]. The vendor claims heavy writers save around 20 hours per month [1]. It is positioned as a practical pick for the AI crowd that wants to actually speed up daily writing rather than just talk about productivity [1].

bullets.label: Privacy angle:
bullets.text: Voicely leads on GDPR compliance, a relevant differentiator for DACH and EU users [1].

bullets.label: Works everywhere:
bullets.text: The speech recognition runs in any app rather than a single editor [1].

bullets.label: The claim:
bullets.text: Roughly 20 hours saved per month for people who write a lot, per the vendor [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: If dictation fits your workflow and EU data rules matter, Voicely (voicely.de) is worth a trial — but treat the 20-hours figure as a vendor claim, not a benchmark [1].

editorial.title: The day the AI stack got picked.
editorial.intro: Two newsletters, two ingested deep-dives and a wall of WhatsApp items, and yet the day has a single shape. Google I/O 2026 set the agenda, and the rest of the industry spent the same 36 hours converging on defaults.
editorial.body: Look at what actually shipped. AMD took 2nm before NVIDIA. OpenAI picked Singapore as its first non-US lab. Anthropic put Mythos behind closed doors and used it to find 10,000 vulnerabilities. Google made SynthID the cross-lab watermark, launched Gemini Spark as a true background agent, extended Gemini Omni into video and wired Project Genie into Street View. Washington pulled back on frontier-model vetting. Different decisions, same direction: the optionality of the last two years is closing and the stack is being chosen — default chip node, default geography, default security posture, default provenance standard, default regulatory floor. Underneath the announcements sits the harder story the German newsletters tell with charts: Microsoft's token bills now exceed salaries, DeepSeek has made a 75% price cut permanent, HBM eats 63% of a chip's cost, seven million H100-equivalents sit outside the famous labs, and Google's token volume is up 330x in two years. The product layer is dazzling; the economics layer is where the constraints live. And on the physical side, EngineAI's 15-minute humanoid cadence and Tesla's million-unit Fremont plan move robotics from demo to throughput.
editorial.pull_quote: The product layer is dazzling. The economics layer is where the constraints live.
editorial.outro: The security thread runs both ways on the same day — Anthropic's Mythos finding 10,000 bugs while a supply-chain attack quietly seeds 700 GitHub repos and Perplexity open-sources a scanner to fight back. Capability and exposure are scaling together.

takeaway.label: IF YOU TAKE ONE THING FROM THIS
takeaway.text: Value over the next 18 months will accrue to operators who adopt the same defaults the labs just picked — and who watch the token bill as closely as the demo. Pick with the stack, but price the compute honestly.
